summary: Baileys WhatsApp library fork — static keyword co-occurrence requires human review
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. A a static rule fired on lib/Utils/generics.js due to keyword co-occurrence (the strings 'ping', 'GET', and 'id') in a file typical of WhatsApp protocol handling — Baileys uses 'ping' as a WebSocket keepalive verb and performs HTTP GETs against WhatsApp endpoints as part of its documented protocol. No concrete attacker-controlled exfiltration destination, credential read, install-time fetch-and-execute, or lifecycle hook was identified. Because this is a third-party fork of a popular library (forks of Baileys have historically introduced covert behavior such as auto-subscribing to the fork author's channels using the installer's WhatsApp session), human review is recommended to confirm the fork does not add covert actions on top of upstream behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
